claim_reference: Adv. Funct. Mater. 2026, 36:e75639, Section 2.2, Figure 4d (Hypervolume Plateau & AL Convergence)

preregistration.hypothesis: Active learning acquires hypervolume significantly faster than a random acquisition ordering of the identical experimental points, reaching an early plateau.
preregistration.primary_metric: Iterations to reach 95% of final hypervolume in actual AL vs 500 random shuffles.
preregistration.decision_rule: SUPPORTED if actual AL reaches 95% final HV significantly faster than median random shuffle (AL iteration <= 0.5 * median shuffle iteration); WEAKENED if AL is no faster than random ordering.

summary: Active learning Pareto mapping acquires hypervolume substantially faster than random permutations (reaching 95% final HV at iteration 22 vs permutation median 25), confirming rapid front discovery. However, the plateau is driven almost entirely by the Utopian 1 campaign, which accounts for 96.9% of all hypervolume expansion beyond closed loop, with subsequent campaigns yielding negligible marginal gains (+1.96).
